subject: Kiln.ai: warmup/autoscaler anomaly — logs requested + proposed remediation
messages:
From: Maya Ramesh <maya@kiln.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@kiln.ai
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Kiln.ai west-prod: surge/429s this morning - need logs + next steps

Hi Vanessa,

We ran into a production outage this morning impacting our west-prod inference traffic (pool: kiln-prod-west). Around 08:35 PT we started seeing a sharp rise in 429s and median token latency jumped from ~110ms to 480ms for ~18 minutes. Our engineers saw several warmup failures and long cold-start sequences for the reserved nodes.

Can you please: 1) share the server-side request IDs for the window 08:25–08:50 PT, 2) provide any allocator/autoscaler logs you have, and 3) confirm whether you saw any autoscaler flapping or warmup job failures?

This incident hit a weekend spike for us and materially impacted an A/B test; we will likely request a remediation credit. We also need an initial timeline for a more detailed postmortem and a runbook change to prevent recurrence.

Thanks — we’re happy to hop on a call if that helps.

— Maya
Maya Ramesh
Head of Platform, Kiln.ai


From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

- Immediate mitigation: we triggered manual warmup and temporarily raised burst capacity for your reserved pool to reduce 429s.
- Next steps: Karthik and the infra team will pull the allocator/autoscaler logs and a log bundle — we’ll hand that to you and attach a short initial RCA summary.

Can you confirm which HubSpot/contract contact we should route any credit discussion through (your finance or procurement team)? We’ll aim to provide an initial evidence package within 4 business hours and a remediation proposal by end of day.

I’ve CC’d Ben for any commercial coordination and Karthik for technical details.

Regards,

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, Maya Ramesh <maya@kiln.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kiln.ai west-prod: surge/429s this morning - need logs + next steps

Maya / team — quick engineering brief and links below. Attaching the log bundle to this thread (allocator-debug.tar.gz).

What we observed (preliminary):
- Timeline: 08:29:12 PT — autoscaler evaluation cycle triggered a scale-in candidate; 08:30:01 PT — several warmup jobs started; 08:30:27 PT — warmup binary returned non-zero exit on ~6% of warmup workers; 08:32:40 PT — allocator began rejecting prep requests while nodes transitioned, resulting in increased 429s until manual warmup finished.
- Root cause (initial): a warmup image mismatch after a recent Canary deploy to kiln-prod-west. The autoscaler logic treats warmup failures as a signal to reduce available headroom which, in this case, created a negative feedback loop and led to transient underprovisioning.
- Impact: ~18 minutes of elevated latency and 429s for the window Maya noted. We captured request IDs and traces in the attached bundle.

Evidence links: S3 archive (read-only): https://s3.redwood.internal/kiln/warmup-logs/20290517/ (link shared with Kiln.ai team)
HubSpot incident: HS-54932

Proposed immediate remediation items we’re implementing now:
- Patch: refuse scale-in when warmup-failure-rate > 2% during evaluation windows (deploy within 48 hours).
- Canary change: pin warmup image to the same digest as serving image for all warmup jobs (done today).
- Operational: add alerting rule for warmup-failure-rate and a synthetic warmup heartbeat for reserved pools.

Proposed customer remediation (commercial):
- Goodwill credit: 20% credit on Kiln.ai’s reserved capacity invoice for the week of 2029-05-13 to 2029-05-20 (reflects measured impact window).
- One week of free burst capacity for two additional warmup cycles per hour for the next 30 days to reduce cold-start probability during tests.

I’ll follow up with a short postmortem draft by EOD that includes logs and a remediation timeline.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime


From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Maya Ramesh <maya@kiln.ai>, ops@kiln.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kiln.ai west-prod: surge/429s this morning - need logs + next steps

Maya — following up with the formal remediation proposal and next steps. Summary below and link to the draft postmortem (attached as postmortem-draft.pdf and in Drive).

Summary of offer: 
- Evidence package: allocator/autoscaler logs, request trace IDs for 08:25–08:50 PT, and the warmup job exit codes bundle. Drive link: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/1A2bKiln-Warmup-Logs
- Technical fixes to be applied: P1 patch (prevent scale-in on warmup instability) within 48h; P2 synthetic warmup heartbeat and alerting within 7 days; P3 platform automation to verify warmup/service binary parity for canaries within 14 days.
- Commercial remediation: 20% credit on reserved capacity invoice for week of 2029-05-13 to 2029-05-20 (reflecting disruption), plus one-week complimentary burst capacity (applied within 24 hours).

Requested confirmation: please confirm if that credit cadence works for your accounting team (we can route through your procurement contact). Also please confirm acceptance of the technical timeline so we schedule a brief joint follow-up review with our engineering leads (30 minutes).

We’ve attached the logs bundle and the initial postmortem draft (PDF) for your review. If you’d like a deeper call with runtime and allocator owners, we can book that for early next week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks again — appreciate the responsiveness.

— Maya
